ownership.summary: AB Electrolux owns AEG. Electrolux acquired AEG Hausgeräte in 1994 and obtained worldwide rights to the AEG brand and corporate name in 2004. AEG is therefore a German-origin brand inside a Swedish listed appliance group, not an independent German appliance company today.

leadership.name: Emil Rathenau
leadership.role: Founder of the original AEG business
leadership.context: Electrolux's AEG history traces the business to Emil Rathenau's 1883 electrical company; the role is historical and does not describe current group governance.

productPortfolio.name: Cordless and canister vacuum cleaners
productPortfolio.positioning: AEG sells cordless stick, handheld and canister floor-care products in selected European markets.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Check the exact regional range, battery, filtration, included tools, manufacturer, origin and warranty.

productPortfolio.name: Laundry appliances
productPortfolio.positioning: Washing machines, tumble dryers and washer-dryers form a major part of AEG's precision-performance appliance position.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Voltage, dimensions, energy labels, installation, connected services and service terms vary by market.

productPortfolio.name: Cooking and kitchen appliances
productPortfolio.positioning: Ovens, hobs, cookers, refrigerators and dishwashers extend AEG across the fitted-kitchen system.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Distributors should verify regional specifications, installation responsibility, energy performance and parts support.

productPortfolio.name: Wellbeing and licensed extensions
productPortfolio.positioning: Electrolux can extend group brands into selected wellbeing or licensed product categories.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: A licensed AEG product may use a different operator, factory and warranty route from core Electrolux appliances.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: Electrolux reports an EMEA/APAC production network spanning Germany, Poland, Italy, Hungary, Romania, Ukraine, Egypt, Thailand, China and Australia.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Do not assign a group factory or country to an AEG model without product-level evidence.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: AEG and Electrolux products can share group technology, procurement or manufacturing resources while remaining separate commercial brands.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Compare the exact model specification, declaration, rating plate and service documentation.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: The AEG name can also be licensed beyond directly operated appliance lines.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Identify the trademark authorizer, legal manufacturer, importer, factory and warrantor for the covered product.

marketsChannels.evidence: AEG is one of Electrolux Group's three main appliance brands and is particularly important in Europe and nearby markets.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Confirm that the target category is officially offered and supported in the destination market.

marketsChannels.evidence: AEG's UK shop terms name Electrolux plc as the local site operator and seller route while identifying AB Electrolux as brand owner.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Copy the actual contracting company from the local terms, invoice and warranty.

marketsChannels.evidence: AEG appliances reach buyers through national sites, appliance retailers, kitchen specialists and service partners.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Verify seller authorization, delivery, installation, returns, parts and warranty coverage.

competitivePosition.summary: World Clean Biz assessment: AEG combines strong German engineering heritage with Electrolux Group scale and a broad European appliance portfolio. The brand can connect floor care to laundry and kitchen categories, but buyers must avoid converting brand heritage or group factory data into a blanket origin claim.
